title: Implement CLI reporting output and error handling
description: Add the user-facing output layer to `src/lumamatch/cli.py`: a compact success report on stdout and single-line actionable errors on stderr with no tracebacks. This is the only UI the tool has, so clarity here is the whole user experience. Every number carries a unit and fixed precision, and the output paths are printed last so they can be copied.
acceptanceCriteria: On success, stdout reports: reference dimensions, target dimensions, bin count, EMD before and after with the percent reduction, clipped-pixel percentage, and both output paths
EMD values print with 3 decimal places and the `L*` unit; percentages print with 2 decimal places and a `%` sign
Output paths are printed last, in full, one per line
`--quiet` suppresses all of the above but still prints errors
A `FileNotFoundError` prints `error: <message>` to stderr and returns exit code 2 with no traceback
A `ValueError` (unsupported format, corrupt file) prints `error: <message>` to stderr and returns 2
A `FileExistsError` prints an error naming the file and mentioning `--force`, and returns 2
A `PermissionError` prints an error naming the directory and returns 2
An unexpected exception still returns a non-zero code and prints a single-line error rather than a raw traceback
Nothing is printed to stdout on any error path
Unit tests assert output content with capsys and assert exit codes for every error class; `ruff check` clean

steps.description: Write the report formatter as a pure function
steps.details: Write `format_report(result: MatchResult) -> str` returning the multi-line report. Making it pure (no printing) means the tests assert on a returned string rather than parsing captured stdout, and the CLI just prints what it returns.

Lines in order: `reference: <path.name> (<W>x<H>, <N> px)`; `target:    <path.name> (<W>x<H>, <N> px)`; `bins:      <bins>`; `EMD:       <before:.3f> -> <after:.3f> L* (<reduction*100:.2f}% reduction)`; `clipped:   <clipped_fraction*100:.2f}% of pixels`; blank line; `wrote <image_out>`; `wrote <csv_out>`. Align the labels so the values form a column.

steps.description: Store the dimensions needed for the report
steps.details: The report needs W and H, but MatchResult only carries pixel counts. Either add `reference_shape`/`target_shape` tuple fields to MatchResult (updating TASK-13's validation and the tests accordingly) or derive the report's dimension text in the pipeline. Prefer adding the two shape fields — the CSV metadata does not need them but the report does, and threading them through the result keeps `format_report` pure.

In `main`, wrap the pipeline call in `try/except`. Catch `(FileNotFoundError, ValueError, FileExistsError, PermissionError, OSError)` as `exc`, print `f'error: {exc}'` to `sys.stderr`, and `return 2`. Add a final `except Exception as exc` printing `f'error: unexpected failure: {exc}'` and returning 1, so a bug still yields a clean message and a distinguishable code.

When `args.quiet` is set, skip the `print(format_report(result))` call entirely. Error printing must be unconditional — quiet suppresses success reporting, never diagnostics. Add a comment stating this so it is not 'simplified' later.

In `tests/test_cli_report.py`, run a real match in `tmp_path` via `main([...])` with capsys. Assert the captured stdout contains 'EMD', '-> ', 'L*', '% reduction', 'clipped', and both output filenames. Assert the EMD figures match `f'{result.emd_before:.3f}'` formatting by regex (three decimals).

Assert `main(['missing.png', str(tgt)]) == 2` with stderr starting 'error:' and stdout empty. Assert the same for an unsupported `.bmp` target, for a corrupt PNG, and for a second run without `--force` (stderr must contain '--force'). Assert a run with `--force` returns 0.
Assert a successful `main([ref, tgt, '--quiet'])` returns 0 and produces empty stdout, while a failing quiet run still writes to stderr and returns 2.
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/ -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`. Visually inspect the real report output once by running the tool on two sample images and confirm the columns align.

technicalNotes: No Playwright, browser, or screenshot verification applies — this is terminal output. Visual verification means reading the printed report once and confirming alignment.
Keeping stdout empty on errors is what makes the tool safe to pipe: a caller can consume stdout without ever parsing an error message as data.
Distinguishing exit 2 (expected/user error) from exit 1 (unexpected bug) gives scripts something useful to branch on.
If step 3 leads to adding shape fields to MatchResult, update TASK-13's tests in the same commit so the suite stays green — do not leave the model and its tests out of sync.
